meta.note: Companion to research/relocating/state-tax-table.md. Tax year 2026 unless a field note says otherwise. RATES ARE DECIMAL FRACTIONS: 0.0399 means 3.99 percent. Bracket arrays are ordered lowest to highest; each entry's 'upTo' is the top of that bracket in dollars of that state's taxable income, and the final entry has upTo: null meaning no ceiling. effectivePropertyTaxRate is median real estate taxes paid divided by median owner-occupied home value, ACS 2024 data, from Tax Foundation's March 16, 2026 table. medianPropertyTaxBill is the ACS 2024 1-year state median (table B25103), which is a different vintage from the effective rate and will not divide out exactly. Local income taxes are EXCLUDED from bracketsSingle/bracketsMFJ/topRate - NY, OH, PA and MD all levy them on top and the omission understates those states. Anything the markdown marks UNVERIFIED is not repeated here as if it were fact. Do not put a figure from this file on a public page without reading the corresponding markdown section first, which carries the caveats.

states.socialSecurityNote: Fully exempt. SC DOR: 'Social Security benefits and railroad retirement taxed for federal purposes are exempt from Individual Income Tax in South Carolina.'
states.retirementExclusionNote: Retirement income deduction under SC Code 12-6-1170(A): up to $3,000/yr of qualified retirement income before age 65, up to $10,000/yr at 65 and after, per taxpayer. Separate age-65 deduction under 12-6-1170(B): $15,000 against any SC income per qualifying spouse ($30,000 when both are 65+), reduced by any retirement or military deduction claimed. All military retirement pay is fully exempt at any age (12-6-1171). H.4216 did not change any of these.
states.vehicleTaxNote: Annual county property tax on vehicles at 6% of fair market value times the full local millage, school operating included. Must be paid before the plate renews. Horry County estimate: $30,000 car about $362/yr unincorporated, about $458/yr in the City of Myrtle Beach, plus a $50 county road maintenance fee. One-time $250 Infrastructure Maintenance Fee when a vehicle first titled in another state is registered in SC; 45 days to register after moving. Standard plate fee UNVERIFIED (dmv.sc.gov blocks automated fetch).
states.movingOutGotcha: Destination state, not an origin. Inbound: 45 days to register vehicles and pay the $250 IMF; apply to the county assessor for the 4% owner-occupied assessment ratio before the first penalty date of the first year claimed, or the home is taxed at 6% with school operating millage included, roughly 3.3x the bill.

states.socialSecurityNote: Fully exempt. NY DTF: 'Social security benefits that are included in federal adjusted gross income may be subtracted from your federal adjusted gross income when computing your New York adjusted gross income.'
states.retirementExclusionNote: $20,000 pension and annuity exclusion at age 59.5 or older, per taxpayer not per return, so $40,000 on a joint return only when both spouses have their own qualifying income. IRA and 401(k) distributions count toward that $20,000 rather than being separately exempt. New York State and local government pensions, federal pensions including military, and certain public authority pensions are fully exempt with no dollar cap and no age test.
states.vehicleTaxNote: No annual property or excise tax on vehicles. Registration is weight-based: $26.00 to $140.00 for TWO years. Plates $25, title $50. County vehicle use tax plus MCTD supplemental fee: NYC $30 use tax plus $50 supplemental per two years; most other counties $10 to $20 per two years. Roughly $13 to $70 a year all in.
states.estateTaxNote: Basic exclusion amount $7,350,000 for deaths in 2026 ($7,160,000 in 2025), rates 3.06% to 16%. A 'cliff' reportedly removes the exclusion entirely for taxable estates above 105% of it (about $7,717,500); that mechanic is from Wealthspire, not restated on the NY DTF page opened 2026-08-16, so treat it as MEDIUM confidence.
states.gasTaxNote: CONTRADICTION, do not publish a figure. Tax Foundation (July 2025) gives 24.87 cents; AARP (March 31, 2026) gives 23.85 cents for 2026. The two count different components of New York's motor fuel excise, petroleum business tax and prepaid sales tax stack. Either way New York is BELOW South Carolina's 28.75 cents, so this is the one origin state where per-gallon state tax goes up on a move. Needs a human check at tax.ny.gov.
states.movingOutGotcha: Two traps. First, domicile: NY DTF says 'Your New York domicile does not change until you can demonstrate with clear and convincing evidence that you have abandoned your New York domicile and established a new domicile outside New York State.' Second, statutory residence: even after a real domicile change, New York taxes you as a full-year resident if you keep 'a permanent place of abode in New York State for substantially all of the taxable year' AND spend '184 days or more in New York State during the taxable year' - so keeping the Long Island house and visiting family half the year can leave a former New Yorker taxed by both states.
states.asOf: 2026 tax year. Standard deduction figures are the 2025 table, which NY does not index, so they carry to 2026. Another 0.1 point comes off the bottom five brackets in 2027.

states.socialSecurityNote: Fully exempt. N.C.G.S. 105-153.5(b)(3) deducts 'Benefits received under Title II of the Social Security Act and amounts received from retirement annuities or pensions paid under the provisions of the Railroad Retirement Act of 1937.'
states.retirementExclusionNote: No general age-based exclusion. Private pensions, 401(k), 403(b), traditional IRA withdrawals and annuities are fully taxed at 3.99%. Two carve-outs: the Bailey settlement exempts benefits from NC and federal government defined benefit plans (and State 401(k)/457 plans) but ONLY for retirees with five or more years of creditable service as of August 12, 1989, a closed and shrinking class; and military retirement pay is exempt for a retiree who served at least 20 years in the uniformed services or was medically retired.
states.groceriesNote: Exempt from the state and transit rates, but a 2.00% local rate applies to qualifying food. Candy, soft drinks, prepared food, dietary supplements and vending-machine food are taxed at the full combined rate.
states.vehicleTaxNote: Annual county vehicle property tax, collected with registration renewal under the Tag and Tax Together program: 'You must pay both your vehicle's registration and the property tax at the same time.' Registration fee for a regular private passenger vehicle is $46.25 per year, effective July 1, 2024, adjusted every four years to CPI (next adjustment due July 1, 2028). Highway Use Tax at titling is 3%, capped at $2,000 only for commercial vehicles and RVs.
states.gasTaxNote: NCDOR 2026 motor fuels rate is 41.0 cents plus a 0.25 cent inspection tax = 41.25 cents. This SUPERSEDES the Tax Foundation July 2025 figure of 40.55 and the AARP figure of 40.3 (which is the 2025 rate).
states.movingOutGotcha: The counterintuitive one: state income tax can go UP. NC is a flat 3.99% with a $25,500 joint standard deduction; SC from 2026 is 1.99% on the first $30,000 then 5.21%, with a deduction that phases out between $80,000 and $190,000 of joint AGI. Arithmetic on the two published schedules (joint, no dependents, no credits) puts the crossover around $100,000 of joint AGI - above that a mover from NC pays more state income tax in SC. Those are internal estimates, not published figures; re-run them before use. Mechanically, leaving NC is simple: a part-year Form D-400 with Schedule PN, and no statutory day-count residency test of the New York or Ohio kind.
states.asOf: 2026 tax year. Further rate cuts possible from 2027 under the N.C.G.S. 105-153.7(a1) revenue trigger; do not publish a 2027 rate.

states.bracketsNote: SIMPLIFIED. Ohio uses one schedule for all filing statuses and has no standard deduction, only personal exemptions ($2,400 single / $4,800 MFJ for 2026, reduced to $2,150 each at $40k-$80k MAGI and $1,900 each above $80k, and lost entirely at MAGI of $500,000 or more from 2026). The statute, ORC 5747.02(A)(3)(c), reads 'For taxable years beginning in 2026 and thereafter, $332.00 plus 2.75% of the amount in excess of $26,050' - a $332 base amount, not a smooth zero-then-2.75% ramp. Do not build a calculator on the two-bracket simplification above without checking the 2026 Form IT 1040.
states.socialSecurityNote: Fully exempt. ORC 5747.01 deducts 'Benefits under Title II of the Social Security Act and tier 1 railroad retirement' from federal AGI.
states.retirementExclusionNote: Pensions, 401(k) and IRA withdrawals ARE taxable at 2.75%. No exclusion, only two small credits under ORC 5747.055, both capped at modified AGI less exemptions below $100,000: a retirement income credit on a sliding schedule topping out at $200 per return ('Only one such credit shall be allowed for each return'), and a $50 per return senior citizen credit at age 65 or older. Ohio's 'retirement income credit' sounds generous and is worth at most $200 a year.
states.groceriesNote: ORC 5739.02(B)(2) exempts 'Sales of food for human consumption off the premises where sold.'
states.vehicleTaxNote: No annual property or excise tax on vehicles. Ohio BMV passenger vehicle registration is $36.00 per year effective 1/5/2026, plus an $8.00 deputy registrar fee for a one-year renewal, plus a local permissive tax that 'cannot exceed $30.00 per vehicle'. Title fee $18 statewide, $23 in some counties. Roughly $44 to $74 a year, none of it tied to vehicle value.
states.estateTaxNote: None. Ohio's estate tax was repealed for deaths on or after January 1, 2013 (repeal date UNVERIFIED at a primary source; the current-year answer of 'none' is confirmed).
states.movingOutGotcha: Ohio's bright-line residency test has one condition that catches almost everybody: you cannot hold an Ohio driver's license or state ID at any point in the year. ORC 5747.24(B)(1) presumes non-domicile for a full year only if you file a statement with the tax commissioner AND have no more than 212 contact periods in Ohio, keep an abode outside Ohio all year, 'did not hold a valid Ohio driver's license or identification card at any time during the taxable year', and claimed no Ohio homestead property tax reduction. The statement is due by October 15 and a false one 'is guilty of perjury'. File it and qualify and the presumption is 'irrebuttable'; fail to file and you are presumed Ohio-domiciled for the entire year. A 'contact period' is any portion, 'however minimal, of each of two consecutive days in this state'.
states.asOf: 2026 tax year (HB 96, 136th General Assembly, effective September 30, 2025). NOTE: Ohio municipalities levy their own income tax (commonly 1% to 3%) and many school districts levy a separate SDIT on top; Tax Foundation puts Ohio's average effective local income tax rate at 1.49%. South Carolina has none.

states.bracketsNote: No standard deduction. Personal exemption $1,000 single / $2,000 MFJ, dependent exemption $1,500. An additional exemption at age 65+ exists but the amount is UNVERIFIED here.
states.socialSecurityNote: Fully exempt. NJ Division of Taxation lists 'Social Security and Railroad Retirement benefits' as nontaxable retirement income.
states.retirementExclusionNote: Pension Exclusion at age 62 or older (or disabled), with a hard income cliff. Total income $150,001 or more: 'Not eligible for a pension exclusion.' Total income $1 to $100,000: exclude taxable pension, annuity and IRA withdrawals up to $100,000 MFJ, $75,000 single/HOH/QW, $50,000 MFS. $100,001 to $125,000: exclude 50% MFJ, 37.5% single, 25% MFS of the taxable pension. $125,001 to $150,000: 25% MFJ, 18.75% single, 12.5% MFS. Military pensions and survivor benefits are exempt at any age; civil service annuities are not. Nonresidents pay no NJ tax on pension, annuity or IRA income at all. Below $100,000 of total income this exclusion is MORE generous than South Carolina's, so a NJ retiree under the cap can pay more income tax after moving.
states.groceriesNote: Most groceries exempt, and New Jersey also exempts most clothing and footwear entirely, which South Carolina does not. Grocery treatment sourced to AARP (April 6, 2026); the nj.gov exemption pages 404'd on 2026-08-16, so MEDIUM confidence.
states.vehicleTaxNote: No annual property or excise tax on vehicles. NJ MVC registration by weight class and model year: $46.50 (under 3,500 lbs, older than 2 years), $59.00 (under 3,500 lbs, within 2 years), $71.50 (over 3,500 lbs, older than 2 years); older model-year classes $35.50 to $72.50. Zero-emission vehicles pay an added annual fee, $250 from July 1, 2024, rising $10 per year for four years. One-time 0.4% fee on new passenger cars costing $45,000 or more.
states.estateTaxNote: None since 2018. NJ Division of Taxation: 'New Jersey Estate Tax is no longer imposed for individuals who died on or after January 1, 2018.'
states.inheritanceTaxNote: Transfer Inheritance Tax based on WHO inherits, not estate size. Class A is fully exempt: parent, grandparent, spouse, child (including legally adopted), grandchild and great-grandchild, stepchild (not step-grandchild), mutually acknowledged child, civil union partner after 2/19/2007, domestic partner after 7/10/2004. Class C (sibling, or spouse/civil union partner of a child) gets a $25,000 exemption then 11% to 16%. Class D (everyone else) 15% to 16%, no exemption. Class E (charities, religious, educational, medical, government) exempt. Most buyers leave to spouse and children, who pay nothing.
states.gasTaxNote: Effective January 1, 2026: PPGRT rose from 34.4 to 38.6 cents plus the fixed 10.5 cent Motor Fuels Tax = 49.1 cents. SUPERSEDES the Tax Foundation July 2025 figure of 44.95.
states.movingOutGotcha: The so-called 'exit tax' is not a tax. It is an estimated Gross Income Tax payment a NON-RESIDENT seller must make before the deed can be recorded (N.J.S.A. 54A:8-8 to 8-10), calculated as the federal reportable gain times the top 10.75% rate but 'not less than 2% of the seller's consideration...stated in the deed', and it is credited or refunded on the New Jersey non-resident return. It is owed even with no gain: 'Even if the seller/grantor do not recognize a gain, they are still required to pay at least 2% of the total consideration stated in the deed on or before the time of closing.' The ordering matters: a seller still resident in NJ at closing files GIT/REP-3 and nothing is withheld; a seller who has already moved to South Carolina files GIT/REP-1 with payment. There is also an IRC Section 121 exemption where the property was a principal residence and the ENTIRE gain is federally excludable.
states.asOf: 2026 tax year. Pension exclusion tiers are the figures NJ publishes against the 2025 NJ-1040; nothing different has been published for 2026 as of 2026-08-16. NJ property tax relief programs (Stay NJ, Senior Freeze, ANCHOR) do not travel and must be netted off before claiming a property tax saving.

states.bracketsNote: No standard deduction and no personal exemption. Pennsylvania has a low-income Tax Forgiveness credit (Schedule SP) whose limits are UNVERIFIED here. Local earned income tax is levied by most municipalities on top of the 3.07%, averaging 1.07% effective statewide and reaching 3.74% in Philadelphia and 3.75% in Chester City.
states.retirementExclusionNote: Pennsylvania taxes NO retirement income once you are retired. PA DOR: 'Under Pennsylvania law, payments commonly recognized as old age or retirement benefits are not subject to tax. In order to be considered exempt retirement benefits, the payments must come from an eligible Pennsylvania retirement plan and must be paid to persons retired from service after reaching a specific age or after a stated period of employment.' Eligible plans include 401(a) qualified pension plans, IRAs, Roth IRAs, SEPs and Keoghs. Military retirement also exempt. The exception is early distributions: those taken 'before retirement age or years of service are taxable in the year received to the extent that the distributions exceed previously taxed contributions.' Note also that PA taxes 401(k) contributions going in - 'Employee contributions to any retirement plan are always taxable as compensation.'
states.groceriesNote: Most groceries exempt, and Pennsylvania also exempts candy, gum and most clothing, which South Carolina does not. Sourced to AARP (March 24, 2026); statute 72 P.S. 7204 UNVERIFIED here.
states.vehicleTaxNote: No annual property or excise tax on vehicles. PennDOT Form MV-70S (4-26): passenger registration $48.00 for one year, $96.00 for two. Certificate of title $72.00. Participating counties add a $5 annual Fee for Local Use. New for 2026, a Road User Charge of $250/yr for electric vehicles and $63/yr for plug-in hybrids. About $48 to $53 a year for a gasoline car, regardless of value.
states.inheritanceTaxNote: Yes, with NO exemption threshold. PA DOR: '0 percent on transfers to a surviving spouse or to a parent from a child aged 21 or younger; 4.5 percent on transfers to direct descendants and lineal heirs; 12 percent on transfers to siblings; and 15 percent on transfers to other heirs, except charitable organizations, exempt institutions and government entities exempt from tax.' Property owned jointly between spouses is exempt. Unlike New Jersey, Pennsylvania taxes transfers to CHILDREN, at 4.5% from the first dollar. Due at death, delinquent nine months later, 5% discount if paid within three months.
states.gasTaxNote: PA DOR 2026 motor fuel tax rate on liquid fuels (motor gasoline and gasohol) is $0.576/gallon, effective January 1, 2026, unchanged from 2025. Tax Foundation's 58.70 for July 2025 is about 1.1 cents higher because it adds other per-gallon taxes and fees; cite whichever you use.
states.movingOutGotcha: Pennsylvania inheritance tax follows Pennsylvania real estate even after you stop being a Pennsylvanian. Section 2116(b)(2) of the Inheritance and Estate Tax Act of 1991: 'When the decedent was a nonresident, the tax shall be computed upon the value of real property and tangible personal property having its situs in this Commonwealth...at the rates in effect at the transferor's death.' Keeping the Bucks County house does not escape it - the estate files Form REV-1737-A and pays at the same 4.5% / 12% / 15% rates. Second, running the other way: Pennsylvania taxes no retirement income at all, so a retiree moving to South Carolina starts paying state income tax on a pension for the first time. Small after SC's deductions, but not zero. Do not claim an income tax saving for a Pennsylvania mover.
